properties.preserved_distinctions: It does not merge the mechanisms behind the shared reliance: es-01 is local and constructive (per-class explicit denominators), es-02 is global and existential (seeks a finite covering), es-10 aggregates local identities into a global density statement, and es-08 is a meta-level obstruction analysis that constructs nothing. Same wall, four structurally different operators.
properties.contrast_check: The partial-success es-12 also builds a congruence system, but it is designed so that 'by construction none of the admitted congruences is a quadratic' residue — i.e., it explicitly routes around this property rather than sharing it, and its remaining gap is self-declared conjectural coverage, not the reciprocity block. es-04, es-09, and es-11 do not source solvability from fixed-modulus congruences at all, so the property discriminates.
properties.falsification: Exhibiting a fixed-modulus polynomial-identity congruence family that provably eliminates a quadratic-residue class (e.g., a covered class in which n is a quadratic residue to the relevant small moduli) would refute the claimed confinement.

properties.statement: The approach spends a finite resource (finite covering family, finite verification range, finite battery of classes) against a survivor set that is demonstrated to be infinite, so exhaustion is structurally impossible rather than merely unfinished.

properties.preserved_distinctions: The finite resources differ in kind: es-02 seeks a finite system of moduli covering Z (existential, global), es-07 enumerates and certifies instances up to a bound (constructive, empirical, per-n), and es-10 assembles many identity-bearing classes to shrink a density (mixed local-to-global). These remain distinct search modes despite the common finite-vs-infinite mismatch.
properties.contrast_check: The partial-success es-12 also proposes a finite congruence system, but its leftover is only conjecturally empty ('coverage of all primes by Type A/B is conjectural'), whereas in the three failed notes the infinite leftover is established. es-04, es-09, and es-11 do not attempt exhaustion by a finite family at all, so the property still separates proven-insufficient finite programs from the open one.
properties.falsification: A proof that the survivor set of one of these finite families is actually finite (for instance, a candidate covering or class battery whose exceptional set is provably finite or empty) would refute the property.

properties.statement: The approach reasons one class or one instance at a time and never couples classes into any global organization of the solution set, leaving it no leverage over survivor classes as a whole.

properties.preserved_distinctions: The local operators are structurally different: es-01 computes denominators by closed-form identity per residue class with no search, es-03 enumerates divisors of an n-dependent quantity with local congruence filters, and es-07 performs bounded exhaustive search with certificates. The property names only the shared uncoupled locality, not a shared construction.
properties.contrast_check: The partial successes are global or mixed in locality: es-04 'cuts across the residue-class families', es-09 lifts the parameterizations onto one unifying variety, es-11 links classes through shared solution forms, and es-12 couples the form view with the covering goal. None is purely class- or instance-local, so the property discriminates failure-side structure.
properties.falsification: Demonstrating that a purely class-local, uncoupled identity or search mechanism certifies an entire infinite quadratic-residue survivor class — or evidence that one of the three cited approaches in fact couples classes globally — would refute the property.

properties.statement: The approach replaces per-n existence with a global quantitative statement (an average or a density) whose growth or decay is intrinsically too weak to force a solution for every prime, so rare survivors are structurally permitted.

supporting_passages.quote: Its boundary is intrinsic to the method: the average grows only polylogarithmically.

properties.preserved_distinctions: es-05 is probabilistic in posture, averaging the solution-count function over primes with sieve machinery (Bombieri–Vinogradov, Brun–Titchmarsh, Turán–Kubilius); es-10 is deterministic, assembling identity-bearing congruence classes and bounding the exceptional density. Averaging solution counts and thinning an exceptional set remain different operations on different objects.
properties.contrast_check: The partial-success es-06 shares the almost-all ceiling ('covers almost all primes but degrades for perfect-square-like primes'), which weakens this property as pure failure structure: it marks a family-wide quantitative ceiling that even a partially successful method hits, rather than a trait unique to the failed notes. It is retained, at lower confidence, because in es-05 and es-10 the too-weak bound is the terminal boundary rather than an intermediate tool.
properties.falsification: Producing an averaging or density argument within this family whose bound is quantitatively strong enough (e.g., the at-least-polynomial growth es-05 says such an upgrade needs) to force existence for every prime would refute the claimed intrinsic weakness.
